did: I gave home's weekly engagement read the friction measures a walkthrough may say: over the last four weeks, how many days each part of the app was opened, how often each step was left and moved on from with the median time in it, and the median of how hard applying felt, with medians from fewer than five values left unsaid. Home keeps no list of modules; the some-ui side maps these rows onto the registry. I then adopted the orphaned some-ui walkthrough branch, fixed what three reviews found (a false 'used a lot' claim, a stale-take hole, a second audio join now shared with the cards essays), filed your two privacy questions as asks, and built your answers: silent modules now say how long they've been quiet, and an opened-days count that would give away fewer than five unopened days is hidden. Both halves landed through the coordinator's buckets, server#1108 and some-ui#3410.

calls.title: Where the walkthrough's friction is worked out
options: Home sends raw counts per part of each module, and some-ui maps them onto its module list
Home works out the per-module figures itself, from a copy of some-ui's module list
calls.why: Only some-ui's registry knows each module's root, which are not measured, and which step is last; a copy on home could drift and call a live module a graveyard.
calls.undo: Move the mapping onto home behind a contract that carries the registry's opened table, keeping the raw rows as its input (call C934).

calls.title: Medians from fewer than five values are not said
options: Home leaves a median of fewer than five values unsaid, and the report writer bands the counts
Home leaves everything raw for the writer
calls.why: A median of one to four values is close to one visit's own time, so withholding it at the source is the safer reading of your ruling C861.
calls.undo: Have home always send medians and let the writer withhold them (call C935).

calls.title: The walkthrough's render on home waits for a later session
options: A new walkthrough render job on home that calls the walkthrough tool with Kokoro
Widen the cards essays' render job to take walkthroughs
calls.why: The cards essay renderer refuses a spoken shot that shows a screen, and walkthroughs are drawn by a different tool; the job also needed some-ui's half first.
calls.undo: Build it as the other option (call C936).

left: Step 3, the walkthrough rendered on home in Studio's Renders, is not built: it needs a render job that writes each take's 'said' line (draft in call C936, note on #3337).
A finer read of 'finished' needs a step's place on its 'taken' event, which waits on your answer to #3367.
